dwarf.e: From Middle English dwergh, dwerw, dwerf, from Old English dweorg, from Proto-West Germanic *dwerg, from Proto-Germanic *dwergaz. Old High German twerc (German, Luxembourgish Zwerg (“dwarf”)).

dwell.e: From Middle English dwellen (“delay, live, remain, persist”), from Old English dwellan (“to mislead, deceive; be led into error, stray”), from Proto-Germanic *dwaljaną (“to hold up, delay; hesitate”).
dwell.g: A period of time in which a system or component remains in a given state.

dweller.e: From Middle English dweller, equivalent to dwell + -er.
dweller.g: An inhabitant of a specific place; an inhabitant or denizen.

dwelling.e: From Middle English dwellynge, dwellyng (“delay, continuance, abode”), equivalent to dwell + -ing.
dwelling.g: A house or place in which a person lives; a habitation, a home.

dwindle.e: Frequentative form of dwine, from Middle English dwynen, from Old English dwīnan (“to waste away”), from Proto-West Germanic *dwīnan, from Proto-Germanic *dwīnaną. It is equivalent to dwine + -le, akin to Old Norse dvena, dvína, Dutch verdwijnen (“to disappear, dwindle”).
dwindle.g: To decrease, shrink, diminish, reduce in size or intensity.
